cases.name: Ellen Lucille Otter Man
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "She was raised in New Town by her parents, Renetta (Smith) and B. George Mandan. Ellen’s grandparents, the late William and Lucy (Little Owl) Smith played a huge part in her early years. Ellen Luci was named after her grandmother who had the traditional name of “Holy Lodge” or Oti Xopini as spoken in NúEta.  At the tender age of one, her grandmother Lucy said, “Ellen will now be known as “Holy Lodge.” She was a member of the Flint Knife “Mé’?cirooga” Clan.

She graduated from New Town High School in 1990. She continued her education at Fort Berthold Community College and transferred to the University of North Dakota where she graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Psychology. She returned to Fort Berthold and worked for Three Affiliated Tribes in child support services.

Ellen was united in marriage to Richard Wilson III and to this union, three children were born: Richard David IV, Eyren Leander, and Rudy LaTrese. Ellen and her family had so much love to share and welcomed raising her little sidekick, ReNaya “Chatz” White. Chatz came to their family at the age of two and always told Ellen that she had chosen Ellen and not the other way around; these two were inseparable.

In 2018, Ellen relocated to sunny Arizona. The family moved to Casa Grande, Arizona where she worked at New Horizon Adolescence Center for a program that serves wellness to ages 6-18. Ellen loved making a difference, sharing her knowledge, and working one on one with clients.

Having lived in North Dakota most of her life, the warmer climate suited her just right. Ellen and her children enjoyed the warmth in the Valley of the Sun and the cacti!  She loved to hike and would drive to various hiking spots to watch the rising of the sun or to see a magnificent sunset. She
had a few favorite hiking friends that would tag along to enjoy this as much as she did; as well as her children.

Luci played a huge part in the lives of all children of her extended family; she truly cared for each one. She is safely in the arms of the Creator, our Lord Jesus Christ."

cases.name: ReNaya Laurelle “Chatz” White
cases.about:
She had just started kindergarten at Desert Willow Elementary School and was described as a happy, energetic, curious, loving girl.

Her obituary said, "ReNaya Laurelle White, “Chatz”, was born January 24, 2017, in Minot, to Lindsay (Vivier) and Valentino White, Jr. She lived with her mom in Williston and with family in Pendleton, Oregon. She had an outgoing personality, like her mom and her dad’s kindness. Her mom passed away in 2017 and her dad in 2021. She was an enrolled member of the Mandan, Hidatsa, Arikara Nation and a descendant of the Spirit Lake Sioux Nation and Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa.

In 2019, Chatz moved to Casa Grande, AZ, and joined the Ellen Otter Man family when she was 2 years old. Ellen and her family had so much love to share and welcomed raising Chatz. She was Ellen’s little sidekick; they were inseparable. Chatz always told Ellen that she chose Ellen and not the other way around. Chatz always looked to her auntie-mom, Rudy to help her get ready for the day. Rudy would wait for Chatz to get off the bus. She was well beyond her tender years in her thinking and analyzing situations.

She attended Central Arizona Campus Preschool and had just started her kindergarten year at Desert Willow Elementary. She was a happy child and experienced so much love from her extended family. Chatz was known to “chat” with just about anyone. She used to tell people she was blessed with special grandmas, and she knew all their names grandma: Needa, Truby, LG, C, B, Caroline, Lodi, Weezer, Mugs, and Sandy. She called Ellen, “grandma Luci, my best grandma”. She would say to grandma Nae Heart “you are my most favorist grandma in the whole wide world.” She was a ray of sunshine and brought a smile to everyone’s face.

She rode a full-sized horse and was even able to lope in the arena by herself. She was becoming an accomplished rider and was pre-registered at Serenity Riders to begin riding lessons. She was going to be a professional barrel racer. She was starting to jingle dance which she called “jingle bells”. Richard “Little Baby Daddy Rich” took time to show her how to jigg. Her favorite song was “My Pink Sunglasses by Miranda Lambert"

cases.name: Rudy LaTrese Wilson
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Rudy LaTrese Wilson, Sákaa’A witituuNAxaasáštA, (Star Loves Her Horse) was welcomed into the world on June 28, 2006, in Williston, ND, to Ellen Otter Man and Richard Wilson III. She was seen as a miracle gifted to us. From an early age, Rudy was a lively and gracious girl.  Rudy attended elementary and middle school in New Town, ND before moving with her family to Casa Grande, AZ, in 2018. She attended Villago Middle School, Grand Innovation Academy, and had just started her third year at Union High School, all in Casa Grande.

Rudy had a good head on her shoulders with a natural strong-willed nature which she carried with maturity and bravery. Rudy was approachable and helpful. It was important to her that people felt seen and heard and she prioritized empathy and understanding. Rudy held an active interest within her community with pride. Her involvement with AMERIND Club included many traditional and moral values. Rudy had made a positive impact on all club members with her natural leadership spirit. Her open mind and innovative ideas provided great insight into methods of how to improve her environment. 

Rudy took solace within her family and friends. Her constant playful and laughable energy was a delight to see when she shared her comical and amusing stories. She liked Hello Kitty and stuffed animals. Rudy loved expressing herself through her wardrobe, footwear, and hairstyles. She admired uniqueness and creativity. She traveled down many artistic avenues including painting canvases and rocks, drawings of mice and teddy bears, and jewelry making. 

Rudy held dreams of becoming a gymnast, a jingle dress dancer, a barrel racer, and even a welder. She adored animals and held a special connection with them. She was a proud dog mom to Gizmo, Scruff, Rio, and Teddy.  Her animals helped her through trying times. In her downtime, she loved to relax by watching her favorite shows: BoJack Horseman and her ultimate favorite Shameless. Her home life included being the world’s most loved “Auntie Mom” to ReNaya. She helped her family by cooking meals and tending to household chores and was famous for her fry-bread.   Rudy was beloved by her family and friends. She will forever live in our hearts."
